problem: Existing object-search and multi-object-search methods assume freely navigable environments with visible targets. They cannot handle settings where doors block paths and targets are hidden inside cabinets or drawers, which needs combined navigation, exploration and manipulation over long horizons.
motivation: Household robots must open doors and search inside articulated objects, so search and manipulation must be integrated in unexplored environments. Flat RL struggles with the long horizon and the enlarged action space, and naive skill chaining suffers from hand-off failures between skills.
key_idea: A hierarchical RL high-level policy over a semantic/panoptic map memory picks among local exploration, frontier exploration, and instance navigation (with auto-triggered interaction) to discovered doors, cabinets and objects, on top of pretrained mobile subpolicies.
insight: Object-instance-level abstraction gives a compact discrete action space (12 actions) that is data-efficient and transfers to new subpolicies and robots. Ablations show that the two exploration subpolicies are complementary: removing frontier drops unseen SR from 95.6 to 66.5, and removing local exploration drops it to 83.6 with a clear SPL drop. Invalid action masking helps SR and SPL and speeds convergence up to 2.5x. The learned policy beats the greedy and SGoLAM+ decision rules mainly in SPL, and SR gaps are small.
method: Mapping module: egocentric semantic map extended to a partial panoptic map with per-episode random instance colors for doors and cabinets. Targets are marked with a special color and found targets are recolored. Coarse 224x224 (6.6 cm) and fine 84x84 (3.3 cm) crops.

Local exploration subpolicy: pretrained RL policy that predicts the direction to the next target and outputs base velocities. It is frozen, run 4 steps in training and 20 at evaluation, and sees doors and cabinets as obstacles.
Global exploration: frontier points sampled and drawn on the map, navigated to with A*. Far points are projected onto a circle around the agent.

Instance navigation + interaction: the one-hot action selects a mapped door, cabinet or target instance (max 10) and A* navigates to a pose in front of it. Closed doors and cabinets automatically trigger an open action. Training uses magic opening with 15% failure to learn retrials, BiRRT in sim testing, and N2M2 on the real robot.

High-level policy: PPO on an SMDP with a 12-D discrete action space, ResNet-18 map encoder, target vector, valid-action vector, and 22-D robot state. Uses adaptive discounting and invalid action masking.
Rewards: +10 per target found, +3 per door opened, -0.1 per collision, and a distance penalty proportional to the number of waypoints or the exploration invocations.

setting.backbone: PPO high-level policy with ResNet-18 map encoder (trained); pretrained frozen local exploration RL policy; BiRRT planner (sim) or N2M2 mobile manipulation policy (real)
setting.training_data: 8 iGibson challenge apartments, 1-6 random target objects, 3 cabinets per scene; magic-action interactions with 15% failure; trained in simulation only
setting.observation: RGB-D + semantic camera (GT semantics in sim, pre-annotated SLAM map in real), pose/localization, target-object vector
setting.action_space: 12-D discrete high-level actions (local explore, frontier explore, 10 instance IDs); subpolicies output continuous base velocities
setting.privileged: Accurate semantic labels, depth and localization, GT object poses in sim and AR markers in real, plus a pre-built annotated map in the real world for semantics and localization

numbers.eval_set_note: 7 unseen apartments, 25 episodes per scene per object count (1-6), 3 seeds

numbers_note: The benchmark is the paper's own novel task (iGibson), so names use 'other:'. Per-object-count results are in Table I but only the averages are recorded.
results: On unseen apartments HIMOS achieves 95.6% SR and 60.6 SPL averaged over 1-6 objects, beating Greedy (92.7/54.5) and SGoLAM+ (93.0/54.8). SR stays above 91% at six objects, and it reaches 23/30 (76.7%) successful episodes in the real world with unseen subpolicies.
limitations: Assumes accurate perception (semantic labels, poses and a pre-built map) with no integrated perception pipeline, and a static environment.
Fixed maximum number of instances (10) in the action space, and subpolicies are not jointly finetuned.
Baselines are strong (Greedy is within about 3 ppt SR), and the real-world evaluation is small (30 episodes, one environment).
builds_on: Schmalstieg et al. 2022 multi-object search exploration policy
